Lines state base-game facts only; where a page also mentions an add-on or Creation Club item, that part was left out.

lines.line: Summary: Big, ape-like brutes with three black eyes, claws that hit hard and a lot of health that comes back fast during a fight. The pale-furred frost trolls live farther north and higher up and are much tougher than the ordinary cave kind. Every troll leaves troll fat behind.

quoted: Trolls are large, ape-like humanoids endowed with three black eyes
Their powerful arms and claws deal massive physical damage.
Trolls are very strong defensively, with high health and the ability to rapidly regenerate all their health during combat.
The locations inhabited by frost trolls are farther north and at higher elevations than those of their generic cousins
sometimes called "cave trolls"
Frost trolls are significantly more powerful
Trolls of any kind will always drop one sample of troll fat upon death.

lines.line: Weak points: Fire is their weak spot: it hurts them and slows their healing, though only for a while, and if you stop hitting them for long enough the healing goes back to normal. Lingering-damage poisons are a good stand-in when you have no fire. Paralysis helps too, because once it wears off a troll takes a long time to get back on its feet.

quoted: Their greatest vulnerability is to fire, which not only damages them but also impairs their capacity to self-heal.

While the use of fire damage against trolls helps against their fast health regeneration, it doesn't stop it completely. Instead, it slows it way down, and if enough time passes between attacks, their health regeneration will go back to normal, pre-fire damage.

Lingering Damage Health poisons (either ones you've found or made) are an effective way of dealing with the health regeneration of trolls, making it an effective replacement if you don't have a good source of fire damage.
Paralysis (either from a poison, spell or enchanting effect) is also a good counter, as trolls have a very long "getting up" animation after the paralysis has worn off.

lines.line: Looks like: A large, ape-like creature with three black eyes. Frost trolls have white fur.

quoted: Trolls are large, ape-like humanoids endowed with three black eyes
They are distinguishable by their white fur.

lines.line: Tips: Keep your health full: a short string of their blows can kill you, and they come in very quick succession. Hit-and-run works badly because they heal, so raise your armor and add fire by spell or enchantment; with several fire-enchanted weapons to pick from, a lighter, faster one may do better than a heavy one. A frost troll always waits on the snowy canyon path to High Hrothgar, whatever your level.

quoted: Keep your health full when fighting trolls, as two or three of their blows can be lethal and occur in lightning-quick succession.
Other tactics are to maximize your armor and incorporate fire damage, whether by spell or enchantment.
If you have more than one fire-enchanted weapon to choose from, lighter, faster weapons may be more effective than heavier, slower ones.
Using hit-and-run or evasive tactics is less effective, given their ability to self-heal.
There are several Frost Trolls that will always be found in the game world, regardless of your level:
One Frost Troll on the path to High Hrothgar, in the snowy canyon portion.

lines.line: Summary: Enormous humanoids met at their camps, where they herd mammoths. They leave you alone until you get too close or harm their mammoths, and they stay at level 32 however strong you are.

quoted: Giants are enormous humanoids with a primitive, albeit very artistic, culture, and can often be found at their camps.
Giants are normally seen herding mammoths; if you hurt their mammoths or threaten them in any way, the giants will attack.
Unprovoked giants are passive creatures.
Giants do not level up with you, but instead have their level set at 32.

lines.line: Weak points: A hostile giant will not walk into water and eventually wanders off if you stay in it, a weakness you can use when you are low level. Frost spells slow it, and the Unrelenting Force shout at full strength (all three words) can knock it down. Standing on a cliff it cannot reach helps you survive, and from a doorway it cannot enter you can pelt it with attacks.

quoted: Hostile giants refuse to enter water, and will eventually walk away if you remain in a body of water.
This weakness can be exploited if you are taking on a giant but are of a low level.
using Frost spells to slow them down
Giants can be ragdolled with all three words of Unrelenting Force
Exploiting the terrain by staying on cliffs where giants can't reach you can help survival rates
hiding in a doorway that it cannot come in from, and pelting it with attacks

lines.line: Looks like: An enormous humanoid dressed in animal hides and furs, in one of three different looks.

quoted: Giants are enormous humanoids
There are three different appearances for giants. Each appearance consists of a different set of animal hides and furs.

lines.line: Tips: A giant warns you first: it shakes its club overhead, then stomps the ground and turns hostile if you keep coming. Early on even a blocked blow can kill you, so dodge; you can sprint straight past a giant as it starts a club slam or a stomp, because those hits land in front of it and not in a wide circle. You can loot a giant's chest in front of it if you do not linger.

quoted: They are not initially hostile, but if you walk too close to them, they will raise their clubs above their heads and shake them at you. If you continue to approach, they will stomp on the ground and become hostile.
Their attacks, even if successfully blocked, can kill you in one hit. Early on, the best defense is dodging their attacks entirely.
It is possible to dodge the club slam (usually performed by the giant while he is running towards you) and the stomp by sprinting directly past the giant as he performs the attack.
but the damage from the attacks are situated directly in front of the giant, not area-of-effect, like what might be expected.
It is possible to loot a giant's treasure chest right in front of them, as long as you don't stay near them long enough to turn them hostile.

lines.line: Summary: Giant spiders that attack on sight, in the wilds and in dungeons, usually in lairs hung with webs. Their poison hurts both health and stamina. The small ones are the easiest, then the medium ones, and the toughest are bigger than a horse.

quoted: Frostbite Spiders are giant arachnids which attack on sight, and can be found both in the wilderness and in dungeons.
Their lairs are often covered in webs, and usually contain web sacs.
the smallest ones are the easiest, followed by the medium sized ones, and the toughest of all are the spiders which outsize a horse.
(spell Frostbite Poison, Health + Stamina Damage, 5 pts for 5 seconds)

lines.line: Looks like: Reddish orange in dungeons and the south of Skyrim, bluish white in the north, ranging from small up to larger than a horse.

quoted: one that tends to appear in dungeons and in the more southern areas of Skyrim is reddish orange, while the ones found in the northern areas tends to be bluish white.
the toughest of all are the spiders which outsize a horse.

lines.line: Tips: They spit venom from range, even when turned partly away from you, and leap in to bite; without poison resistance almost every hit poisons you. The biggest can outrun you on foot even at a sprint, so you would need a horse to get away. Two giant ones sometimes fight over a corpse in the wild, but if one survives or they spot you first they turn on you. They drop frostbite venom.

quoted: When at range they spit poisonous venom (spell Frostbite Poison, Health + Stamina Damage, 5 pts for 5 seconds), even if turned partly or fully away from their victims, and can leap onto their targets to attack with their bite.
Without poison resistance, you will be poisoned by nearly every hit from these monsters.
The largest of the frostbite spiders can easily outrun you if you attempt to get away on foot without the aid of a horse, even if you sprint.

Two giant frostbite spiders can be found in a random encounter in the wilds, fighting over a non-lootable desicated corpse. If one of the spiders survives (or if they notice you before they kill each other), one or both will turn on you, instead.
Loot: Frostbite Venom

lines.line: Summary: Dangerous half-crone, half-bird creatures that claw you up close and cast destruction magic from afar, often area spells such as Fireball. They show up alone or in threes, often with the Forsworn or in hidden groves and lairs.

quoted: Hagravens are a horrific cross between an old crone and a bird.
extremely dangerous and equally hostile up close or when casting various Destruction spells from afar, usually preferring area-of-effect spells such as Fireball.
Hagravens will tend to appear either individually or in groups of three.
They can often be found in the company of the Forsworn, or dwelling in secret groves and lairs in the wilderness

lines.line: Weak points: Their claws are slow and simple to sidestep, and they turn and walk slowly, so a character of low level can win just by stepping back after each swing of their own. Ice-magic hagravens are the easier kind because they have no area spell.

quoted: It's also worth noting that a hagraven's claw attack is rather slow and easy to dodge. It is entirely possible, and somewhat easy, for even a low level character to defeat one just by moving back slightly after every time you take a swing at them. Hagravens also have a slow turning speed and even slower walking speed, which can also be taken into consideration.
Ice magic hagravens are easier to deal with than fire-based ones, as the ice-based hagravens lack an area-of-effect spell.

lines.line: Looks like: Part old crone, part bird.

quoted: Hagravens are a horrific cross between an old crone and a bird.

lines.line: Tips: A heavily armored warrior can charge in, since armor guards against their claws better than against their spells; with strong elemental resistance, keep your distance and use ranged attacks instead. A hagraven always drops hagraven feathers and sometimes a claw.

quoted: Heavily armored warriors may find it easier to charge in and fight toe-to-toe, because your armor will better protect you against their claws than their Destruction spells. Characters with more elemental resistance might wish to hang back and fight from a distance for similar reasons.
Hagraven Feathers (1 × 100%)
Hagraven Claw (1 × 25%)

lines.line: Summary: Nature spirits that look like glowing green women, mostly wood. They heal themselves, call animals (even normally peaceful ones) to fight for them and summon insect swarms. They hide in foliage with an invisibility spell and strike as you pass, and some step out of tree trunks.

quoted: Spriggans are malevolent nature spirits appearing as glowing, green humanoid females made mostly of wood.
They can restore themselves to full health easily, and can call various animals to aid them in battle, even normally non-hostile creatures such as foxes and deer.
Spriggans also have the ability to summon swarms of insects to attack.

Spriggans can be an unwanted surprise in seemingly peaceful caves and clearings, as they blend in with the foliage using an invisibility spell, then attack when you pass them. Some even seem to inhabit the trunks of trees, stepping from within them when someone comes too close.

lines.line: Weak points: Fire is their weakness. Their big self-heal seems to work only once a fight; just before and while they crouch to heal they resist most damage, so little lands until they get back up.

quoted: They are weak to fire.

Although they are able to heal much of the damage you have done with a special ability, it seems that they can only do this once during battle; they may crouch down multiple times when you bring them to the critical point, but they will no longer keep self-healing.

Though they are able to negate much damage done to them while they are crouched and healing, they have a stage before that point that the ability activates while they are still up and fighting, resulting in most damage being resisted until they get up from their bleedout.

lines.line: Looks like: A glowing green, woman-shaped figure that is mostly wood. Glowing insects around its body stay visible even when it turns invisible.

quoted: Spriggans are malevolent nature spirits appearing as glowing, green humanoid females made mostly of wood.

Although spriggans can cast an invisibility spell on themselves, the glowing "insects" that inhabit their bodies are still visible, allowing you to see where the spriggan is even after they cast the spell.

lines.line: Tips: Its poison spray reaches much farther than a Flames spell and does more damage when cast with both hands. A green flash across the screen means it has called wildlife to fight you, and staggering it mid-cast does not stop that. Its loot is taproot.

quoted: The poison spray that spriggans use has a very long range, much longer than the elemental Novice-level Destruction spells (like Flames). They can also cast it with both hands, resulting in more damage to you.

When the screen lights up with green is when the spriggan has used the ability that calls wildlife to their side, and to fight you. Even if you manage to stagger them just as they are casting it (a flash of green emanates from their body), it doesn't stop the ability from taking effect.
Loot: Taproot, Burnt Spriggan WoodDB

lines.line: Summary: Two of the smaller machines met in Dwarven ruins. Spiders are small, agile and very common, often busy mining or repairing things. Spheres were built for combat: they patrol rolled up in a ball until they meet a threat, then unfold into a half-humanoid shape. Either kind can wait inside pipe ports in the walls and ceilings and spring out as you pass.

quoted: Dwarven spiders are small, arachnid-like automatons, and are very common in Dwarven ruins.
They tend to be found mining or working on building or maintaining various objects that are found in their ruins.
Dwarven spheres are constructs that, unlike Dwarven spiders, were intentionally designed for combat.
These spheres patrol Dwarven ruins in a condensed spherical form until they encounter a threat, at which point they rise into their semi-humanoid form and attack.

They can also be found hiding inside of pipe ports along the walls and ceilings of these ruins where they will lay in wait until they notice something walk by, after which they will leap out and attempt to engage whatever alerted them.
Like Dwarven spiders, they can hide in Dwarven pipes and exit through ports to attack unsuspecting foes that wander too close.

lines.line: Weak points: Shock spells do normal damage to them, while frost and poison do nothing, and they turn aside a quarter of magic damage. Paralysis does not work on them. Unrelenting Force can knock a spider over; no other kind of automaton falls to it that way.

quoted: Furthermore, contrary to what one might expect from reading Ruins of Kemel-Ze, Dwarven automatons are not immune to shock, which actually causes them normal damage. Instead, they are immune to frost and poison damage, and boast a 25% resistance to magic.
Automatons are immune to paralysis, cannot be ragdolled (except for Dwarven spiders), cannot be reanimated, cannot be soul trapped, and have a permanent Waterbreathing ability.
They are also the only kind of automaton that can be ragdolled with Unrelenting Force.

lines.line: Looks like: Spiders are small and arachnid-like, and the stronger ones have electrical effects crackling from their core. A sphere rolls as a ball and rises into a half-humanoid shape to fight.

quoted: Dwarven spiders are small, arachnid-like automatons, and are very common in Dwarven ruins.
These variants are easily distinguished from workers both by name and by the electrical special effects that emanate from their core.
These spheres patrol Dwarven ruins in a condensed spherical form until they encounter a threat, at which point they rise into their semi-humanoid form and attack.

lines.line: Tips: Spiders above level 7 fire short-range electric jolts and burst with more shock damage a moment after they die, and any spider can leap at you to close the gap. Higher-level spheres shoot darts from arm-mounted crossbows and lunge so fast they are hard to sidestep. Both kinds drop scraps, Dwarven oil and soul gems.

quoted: Variants of the dwarven spider higher than level 7 have access to short-range electric jolts that deal shock damage, and will explode a moment after being killed to deal further shock damage.
can also perform a leap attack that will both deal greater damage and close the distance between them and their target
Basic Dwarven spheres utilize only melee attacks, but higher level variants use their arm-mounted crossbows to shoot powerful darts at targets with whom they aren't engaged in melee combat.
their attacks involve a number of very speedy lunges that can close the distance between them and a target rapidly and are very hard to sidestep.
Dwarven spiders can be looted for Dwarven scraps, a very small chance at precious gems, metal ore, Dwarven Oil, and soul gems once killed.
When you kill a Dwarven sphere, you will find a number of items on its remains including Dwarven metal scraps, a small chance at precious gems, Dwarven Oil,

lines.line: Summary: The biggest and strongest machines left in the Dwarven ruins, and usually the ruin's boss. A centurion hits as hard as a dragon can and has a steam breath that works like a shout. Most stand still in a charging gantry until you come near, a lever is pulled or you shoot them from range, and some are used as traps.

quoted: Dwarven centurions are the largest and strongest creations the Dwemer left behind after their disappearance.
formidable enemies that typically serve as the boss of their dungeon
In addition to their incredibly strong melee attacks which can be on par with those of a dragon, they can unleash a powerful steam breath attack that functions like a shout.

Usually centurions are not found simply wandering around a Dwarven ruin, but instead are found immobile within their charging gantries until they are activated either by proximity, lever, or being attacked at range.
In some cases these great constructs are even used as traps to prevent any would-be treasure hunter from plundering the ruins they protect.

lines.line: Weak points: Stand right against its legs: it cannot lower its arms or tilt its head to hit anything beneath its shoulders. Unrelenting Force staggers it, and used before it wakes it can leave the centurion inactive for a while so you can strike freely. Shock does normal damage, while frost and poison do not hurt it.

quoted: If you are a low-level melee character, a surprisingly effective strategy is to get as close to them as possible, to the extent that your character is physically touching the centurion's legs. This is effective because centurions cannot lower their arms or tilt their heads to attack enemies beneath their shoulders, thus enabling you to encircle them and avoid their attacks with relative ease.
they are immune to nearly all shouts except for Unrelenting Force, which causes them to stagger, and Marked for Death.

Sometimes when using Unrelenting Force on a centurion before it has activated from within its gantry, it can be rendered inert and it will not activate immediately, enabling you to strike it at will for a time.

Furthermore, contrary to what one might expect from reading Ruins of Kemel-Ze, Dwarven automatons are not immune to shock, which actually causes them normal damage. Instead, they are immune to frost and poison damage, and boast a 25% resistance to magic.

lines.line: Looks like: A huge, heavily armored warrior shape: one arm ends in a hammer and the other in a battleaxe on a spring.

quoted: Designed in the form of a massively armored warrior with a hammer on one arm and a spring-loaded battleaxe on the other

lines.line: Tips: A ranged attacker gets a few shots in while it is still powering up. Or get it stuck outside a small hallway, stay out of its steam range and shoot or cast at it from there. Its remains hold a guaranteed Centurion Dynamo Core, plus a grand soul gem, Dwarven scraps, arrows and a few gems.

quoted: This can oftentimes give ranged attackers a chance to get a few shots in with either their bow or a spell before the automaton can fully activate and engage in melee range.
Another great strategy is to get them stuck outside of a small hallway and get out of range of their steam attack, allowing you to hit it with ranged attacks.
When defeated, a centurion can be looted for a guaranteed Centurion Dynamo Core, a Grand Soul Gem, a number of Dwarven scraps, leveled arrows, and a few precious gems.

lines.line: Summary: Medium to large earwig-like creatures of swamps, marshes and deep caverns, often kept by Falmer for their chitin. They spit a strong acidic poison that quickly eats through most armor, they climb walls and they have lots of health.

quoted: Chaurus are medium-to-large, hostile, earwig-like creatures found in swamps, marshlands, and deep underground caverns.
They vigorously project a strong acidic poison (spell Chaurus Spit, 7 pts for 7 seconds), which can quickly eat through most armor.
They can cling to walls and have large amounts of health.
Chaurus are often found in the company of Falmer, who breed them for their chitin.

lines.line: Weak points: They avoid crossing water, even knee-deep, so arrows and spells from range work well. Their poison lands less often when you fight them up close, so melee is a sound plan.

quoted: Chaurus (of all varieties) don't like to cross water (knee- or swimming depths), making archery or magic from a distance viable combat options.
The suggestion to use melee force against them seems well-founded, because they are less likely to poison you with their melee attacks.

lines.line: Looks like: An earwig-like insect, medium to large in size.

quoted: Chaurus are medium-to-large, hostile, earwig-like creatures found in swamps, marshlands, and deep underground caverns.

lines.line: Tips: A resist-poison effect only helps if you apply it before the poison damage begins, so carry cure poison potions and use one quickly after a hit. You can also coat your own weapon with poisons, especially ones that weaken, slow or paralyse the target. The poison keeps working after the chaurus is dead, so watch your health. You cannot eat chaurus, and the chitin they drop is used only in smithing.

quoted: Defending yourself with the resist poison effect (only useful if applied before poison damage begins)
Addressing poison damage as quickly as possible after you are hit, with cure poison potions
Poisoning your own weapon repeatedly with toxins you can create, find, or buy, especially if you have powerful effects available such as Weakness to Poison, Slow, Paralysis, etc.
Poison continues to work over time. If you've been hit, watch your health level even after you have killed a chaurus, or your last laugh may be short-lived.
you cannot eat Chaurus yourself. The chitin they drop can only be used in smithing.

lines.line: Summary: Hostile frost spirits that fly fast, circle you and hit with strong frost attacks. They live in cold, snowy places, often in Winterhold and the Pale, and are drawn to standing stones and Nordic ruins.

quoted: Ice Wraiths are hostile frost spirits. They fly quickly, circling the player and attacking with strong frost-based attacks, and are generally found in snowy, cold areas.
They are attracted to standing stones and other Nordic ruins that dot the landscape of Skyrim
Ice Wraiths can often be encountered in the snowy regions of Winterhold and The Pale.

lines.line: Weak points: Fire hurts them extra, and Dawnbreaker and Turn Undead also work on them. Frost does nothing to them, since they resist it fully.

quoted: They are vulnerable to fire attacks, Dawnbreaker, and Turn Undead.
Weakness to Fire, 25 pts
Resist Frost, 100 pts

lines.line: Looks like: Wispy, flying spirits of frost.

quoted: Due to their wispy nature, they have a tendency to ignore the landscape, and can become stuck or die on elevated areas.
Ice Wraiths are hostile frost spirits.

lines.line: Tips: A bite drains stamina, about 21 over three seconds. They also cast a weak wall of frost when attacking or closing in on you, but not while wandering or moving away. They ignore the terrain and can get stuck, or even die, on high ground. Even though they fly, they set off runes. They drop ice wraith teeth and essence.

quoted: indicates stamina damage (7 per second, 21 damage overall) done over a 3-second period.
Ice Wraiths cast a low damage wall of frost-type spell when they attack, and sometimes when they are moving towards you, though never when they are roving the wilderness or moving away from you.
Due to their wispy nature, they have a tendency to ignore the landscape, and can become stuck or die on elevated areas.
Although Ice Wraiths "fly", they still set off runes, such as fire runes.
Ice Wraith Teeth
Ice Wraith Essence

lines.line: Summary: Elemental Daedra that you often meet when an enemy spellcaster has called them up, though you can conjure them too. None of the three kinds can be paralysed, raised as undead servants or turned invisible.

quoted: Atronachs are intelligent elemental Daedra that can be called forth from Oblivion to serve a conjurer in battle against his or her foes.
Atronachs are all immune to paralysis, cannot be reanimated, and cannot be made invisible by any means.
Storm Atronachs can be encountered as a hostile enemy, usually summoned by an enemy caster, or you can summon them to aid in combat.
While typically found in the employ of enemy spellcasters, the player can also conjure them and use them in battle.
They can be summoned by you, and are occasionally used against you by enemy conjurers.

lines.line: Looks like: Flame atronachs look like women made of fire in black metal armor. Frost atronachs are oversized humanoids of solid ice. Storm atronachs are the pieces of a shattered statue circling an unseen, electrified centre.

quoted: Flame Atronachs appear as female humanoids engulfed in flame, wearing intricate, black, metal armor.
Frost Atronachs are Daedric constructs of solid ice that resemble oversized humanoids.
They appear as a shattered statue, the cluster of its remains quickly revolving around an unseen, electrified center of mass.

lines.line: Tips: The flame atronach is the weakest of the three and very agile: it prefers to cast fire from a distance and tries to avoid melee. The frost atronach has a long reach and usually staggers you, but it has no ranged attack, and once you are in reach its chilling cloak slows you. Storm and flame atronachs hover, so they can walk on water. Unbound ones leave fire, frost or void salts. You cannot soul-trap atronachs you summoned yourself, but you can trap another caster's.

quoted: Though they are the weakest type of atronach encountered in Skyrim, they are extremely agile and reasonably proficient in close combat. Flame Atronachs prefer to use their flame-based magic at a distance and will actively try to avoid melee combat if at all possible.

They have a long melee reach and their attacks usually stagger targets, but they are entirely lacking in ranged options. Still, once caught in melee range of them, their chilling cloak slows targets and prevents easy escape.
Like Flame Atronachs, the Storm Atronach hovers and thus has the Waterwalking ability.
When slain, unbound Flame Atronachs will drop Fire Salts, an alchemical ingredient.
Upon death, unbound Frost Atronachs will have Frost Salts on their remains that can be looted.
In the destroyed remains of unbound Storm Atronachs, you will find Void Salts that you can take.
you can no longer soul trap your own summoned Atronachs or Dremora to fill soul gems, although you can soul trap the summoned beings of another caster.
